features.name: Open the MLflow run at the start of the flow
features.description: Today the MLflow run is opened inside the register task, after training has finished, so nothing can be logged while a model trains. Move tracking-URI/experiment setup and run creation to the start of the train flow so every task logs into one active run; trainers can then log per-epoch metrics (needed for YOLO and Hugging Face). Done when: register no longer calls mlflow.start_run, params are logged before training begins, and a metric logged from inside Trainer.train() appears in the same run as the final metrics.
features.evidence: 2026-11-19: ./init.sh green (exit 0). The train flow (pipeline/flow.py) sets the tracking URI/experiment from env, then opens the run inline with `with mlflow.start_run(run_name=cfg.model.name):` and logs the flattened YAML params before any task runs; the with-block ends the run FINISHED, or FAILED on an exception (user's version, replaces the earlier tasks.start_run helper, now removed). register(metrics, trainer) (cfg dropped; agreed with user) no longer calls mlflow.start_run. get_trainer(config) now takes only the config and reads config.model.name (user change). LogisticRegressionTrainer.train() logs train_accuracy (0.961); init.sh asserts exactly 1 FINISHED run containing train_accuracy alongside accuracy 0.295 / f1 0.291, params, and the logged model (pyfunc and trainer.load reload OK). Not in scope: retrain flow (still a stub, opens no run).

features.name: Model saving and champion loading behind the Trainer interface
features.description: Nothing saves or loads a model yet, and the MLflow flavor differs per model (sklearn, transformers, custom pyfunc for YOLO). Add an abstract Trainer.log_model() that logs the trained model to the active run in its own flavor; register calls it without knowing the flavor (inside the run register opens today; inside the flow-level run once feat-001 lands). Extend Trainer.load() so it can start from the current MLflow champion instead of fresh/pretrained weights (prerequisite for the retrain flow). Ask the user before fixing the method signatures (CLAUDE.md rule). Done when: a train run stores a model artifact, it reloads with mlflow.pyfunc.load_model and predicts, and LogisticRegressionTrainer can load() from a logged model.
features.evidence: 2026-11-18: ./init.sh green. Train flow on data/cifar10-mini logged run (accuracy 0.295, f1 0.291) plus model models:/m-85297726798f49648c87c52ef475d424 via LogisticRegressionTrainer.log_model() (sklearn flavor) called from register; it reloads with mlflow.pyfunc.load_model and predicts ('dog' on its input example); LogisticRegressionTrainer.load(model_uri) loads it and gives the same prediction. Both reload checks are now part of init.sh. Signature agreed with user: load(model_uri: str | None = None); the caller resolves the URI (e.g. models:/<name>@champion), trainers never query the registry. Not in scope: champion alias/promotion and the retrain flow.

features.name: Lazy-import trainers in model_factory
features.description: model_factory.py imports every Trainer class up front, so once YOLO and DINO are real, running logistic regression will import torch/ultralytics/transformers and fail if they are not installed. Make TRAINERS map names to import paths (or otherwise defer the import) so get_trainer imports only the requested trainer's module. Keep the existing behavior: classes not instances, unknown name raises an error listing valid names. Done when: running the logistic_regression config does not import trainers.yolo or trainers.dino (check sys.modules), and an unknown name still raises the listing error.

features.name: Tasks pass artifacts instead of sharing the in-memory trainer
features.description: preprocess and train return nothing useful; they mutate the trainer object and the next task reads it. That only works in one process and defeats Prefect task retries, caching and distributed task runners. Change the hand-offs to artifacts: preprocess returns a manifest path, train returns a checkpoint/model URI, evaluate rebuilds what it needs from those. This is the largest change; do it last and ask the user before fixing task signatures (CLAUDE.md rule). Done when: each task's inputs and outputs are paths/URIs or plain data (no live model object crosses a task boundary), and evaluate works on a trainer constructed fresh from the artifacts.

features.name: ROC/AUC in evaluate
features.description: Make the evaluate task also score ROC/AUC on the test split and log the ROC plot. Trainer gains a `classes: Sequence` attribute (column order of predict_proba) and an abstract predict_proba() (no arguments, shape (n_test, n_classes)); evaluate stays model-agnostic and uses only y_test, classes, predict() and predict_proba(). Done when: evaluate returns test_roc_auc (macro one-vs-rest roc_auc_score), one matplotlib figure with a one-vs-rest ROC curve per class (legend with class name and AUC, chance diagonal, macro AUC in the title) is logged as roc_curve.png to the active run, and init.sh asserts both.
features.evidence: 2026-11-20: `./init.sh` exit 0, end-to-end step ran (no SKIPPED). The single FINISHED run has metrics.test_roc_auc = 0.745722 (accuracy 0.295, f1 0.291 unchanged) and init.sh prints 'ROC OK: test_roc_auc=0.7457, roc_curve.png logged' after asserting roc_curve.png is in mlflow.artifacts.list_artifacts(run_id=...). PNG from a separate run downloaded and checked by eye: 10 labelled class curves (AUC 0.583 bird to 0.837 frog), dashed chance diagonal, legend in the lower right without covering the curves. matplotlib added with `uv add matplotlib`; the figure uses matplotlib.figure.Figure (no pyplot, headless-safe). Dino/Yolo predict_proba are NotImplementedError stubs.

features.name: Retrain fine-tunes any model given by URI
features.description: The retrain flow used to mean 'fine-tune the current champion'. It now fine-tunes any MLflow model: the URI comes from model.uri in the YAML (ModelConfig.uri, optional) or from the model_uri flow parameter / `main.py --retrain --model-uri`, and the CLI/flow parameter overrides the YAML (dataset_uri overrides data.uri the same way). If neither is set, retrain raises before opening an MLflow run. Overrides are applied to cfg before params are logged, so the run's params show what actually ran. tasks.train(trainer, model_uri=None) passes the URI to Trainer.load(); trainers make load(model_uri) a real fine-tune start (LogisticRegressionTrainer sets warm_start=True and applies the YAML params). Done when: retrain without any model URI fails with a clear error and opens no run; retrain with --model-uri models:/<registry_name>/1 finishes, logs params.model.uri, and registers a new version; init.sh asserts all three.
features.evidence: 2026-11-25: `./init.sh` exit 0, end-to-end steps ran (no SKIPPED). Train run registered logistic_regression_cifar10 v1 @champion (test_f1 0.3028). `main.py --config configs/train.yaml --retrain` (no model.uri, no --model-uri) exited non-zero with 'retrain needs a model to fine-tune' and opened no run (run count stayed 1). `--retrain --model-uri models:/logistic_regression_cifar10/1` finished as run retrain-logistic_regression-2026-11-25-18:23:42 with params.model.uri = models:/logistic_regression_cifar10/1 and registered v2 from that run. Warm start checked separately: after load(uri) and fit with max_iter=1 the coefficients stay at the loaded model's (max abs diff 0.0000) while a fresh max_iter=1 fit differs by 1.126. init.sh also updated for the configs/example.yaml -> configs/train.yaml rename.

features.name: Retrain gating on the new test split
features.description: register() promotes a new version only if its test_f1 beats the champion's logged test_f1. For train that is fair, but after retraining on a new dataset the champion's logged metric was measured on a different (old) test split, so the comparison is invalid. In the retrain flow, also score the current champion on the same new test split and gate on that. Note the base model (model.uri) may not be the champion. Ask the user before changing task signatures (CLAUDE.md rule), e.g. how evaluate scores a second model and how register receives the champion's score. Done when: on a retrain with a dataset whose test split differs from the champion's, promotion is decided by the champion's and the new model's test_f1 on that same split, and init.sh asserts it.
